mode: codex exec (Codex CLI 0.169.0), built-in imagegen, four runs with one palette sheet attached to each
replaces: Version 1 was eight 128 px pixel-art tiles. The owner found them too simple, so this set looks photographed and worn.
reference: A sheet of eight flat swatches: rust #AA604B, bruise #69404B, chitin #343C3B, olive #777648, teal #418B90, cream #E8D4A6, night #080B08, wing #A4B5A0.
shared:
Use your built-in image generation tool to make texture images for a low-poly 3D research office in a PC game from 1998. Generate each texture as its own image. Save each one as a PNG in the current directory with the exact file name given. Then reply with one line per file: the file name and the path you saved.

The attached image is the colour palette. Keep every texture inside this family of colours: rust, bruised mauve, dark gray-green, olive, pale gray-green, cream, near-black, and teal only where named. Muted and a little dirty. Not saturated.

Shared style for every texture: it must look like a photograph of a real, used surface that an artist in 1998 scanned, cropped, and reduced to a small game texture. Photographic source, not a drawing and not cartoon pixel art. Low resolution with hard square pixels, as if 256 pixels across and scaled up without smoothing. A limited palette of about 48 colours with some dithering. Real wear: scuffs, scratches, stains, dents, chipped paint, grime in the corners. Flat, straight-on view that fills the whole image edge to edge. No perspective, no scene, no border, no frame, no vignette, no cast shadow from outside, even flat lighting. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, logos, brand marks, or readable symbols anywhere: where a real surface would carry a label, show a blank plate, plain bars, or scribbles.
processing: Each result was resized with nearest-neighbour sampling to the size of its place: 256 px for a tile that repeats, and the size of its cell in assets/3d/office/atlas.json for a prop texture.
Each texture was reduced to a 16 colour palette with no dithering. The vending machine keeps 32 colours and the pinboard 24.
office-atlas.png holds every prop texture as one indexed PNG. One white cell serves parts with a plain colour.

office-wall.png is 256 by 512 px and runs once from the ceiling to the floor. The plaster fills the upper part and the wainscot the lowest unit. A script then drew a panel seam with rivets at each edge, one cross seam, dirt toward the floor, and dust under the ceiling.
The screen, the vending machine, the notes, and the wall chart were read at full size, and the rest on contact sheets. None carries a letter, a number, or a logo.

assets.prompt: worn linoleum floor seen from straight above, a 2 by 2 grid of square tiles that fills the image exactly, thin dark seams on the centre lines and on the outer edges. Two tiles pale gray-green and two tiles dull olive, in a checker. Speckled linoleum pattern, black heel scuffs, drag marks, a few dried stains, dirt in the seams. Seamless tiling edges.

a 2 by 2 grid of square acoustic drop-ceiling tiles that fills the image exactly, with a thin off-white metal grid bar on the centre lines and on the outer edges. Tiles are off-white gone yellow-gray, with fine fissures and pinholes. One tile has a brown water stain with a darker rim. Dust near the grid. Seamless tiling edges.

painted plaster wall, cream paint gone dingy, faint roller marks, hairline cracks, old drips, a few smudges and scuffs, slight mottling. One plain surface with no seams, no objects. Seamless tiling edges.

assets.part: wainscot, the lowest unit of the wall
assets.shape: wide, twice as wide as tall
assets.prompt: the lower band of an office wall. Olive painted sheet-metal wainscot, with a dark rust-coloured rail along the top edge, and a dark rubber skirting strip along the bottom edge. Kick marks, scuffs, chipped paint, and dirt that gathers toward the bottom. Tiles seamlessly left to right.
poured concrete wall of an industrial test chamber, dark gray-green, faint horizontal formwork lines, a few round tie holes, vertical water stains, rust streaks. Seamless tiling edges.

painted sheet metal of old office furniture, plain mid gray with a faint green cast, fine brushed scratches, small dents, chipped paint at spots that shows darker steel, a few rust specks. One plain surface with no seams and no handles. Even tone so it can be tinted. Seamless tiling edges.
worn desk-top laminate with a warm rust-brown wood grain that runs left to right, scratches, one faint coffee ring, a few chips. One plain surface. Seamless tiling edges.

the glass face of an old CRT monitor that shows a science readout. Near-black background with a faint glow. Teal and cream phosphor: a jagged line graph in the upper half, a row of vertical bars in the lower half, a small ring gauge in one corner, and short plain dashes where text would be. Faint scanlines and slight blur of the phosphor. No readable characters of any kind.

On the right a column with a coin slot, a blank dark display, and two columns of plain square buttons with nothing on them. A dark delivery flap along the bottom. Scratches, dents, grime. Every packet and plate is blank: no words, no letters, no logos.

worn woven office-chair fabric, bruised mauve, coarse weave, pilling, a pale worn patch and one dark stain. One plain surface.
preserved biological tissue in a specimen jar, seen close: pale wrinkled flesh with folds, mottled cream, rust and mauve, faint veins. One plain surface that fills the image. Not gory, no blood.

A large anatomical drawing of a housefly from above in dark ink with muted rust and teal tints: head with compound eyes, thorax, wings with veins, six legs, abdomen. Thin leader lines run from parts of the fly to small empty boxes. A smaller side-view drawing of the fly below. Fold creases, a torn corner, tape at the top corners.
